decisions.reason: Zogmaister et al. (2020) explicitly retest reference [5] (Bernard, Gervais, Allen, Delmée, & Klein, 2015, Psychology of Women Quarterly, 39(4), 432-446, 10.1177/0361684315580125) in Study 1 (direct replication using counterbalanced stimulus orientation as in [5] Study 1) and Study 2a (conceptual replication with new stimuli), testing whether the body-inversion effect is present for both sexes but significantly stronger for sexualized male than female targets (H1) and unmoderated by participant gender (H1b), and evaluating their Study 1 and Study 2a results against both [4] and [5] in the Discussion sections. Shipped row 853 (Bernard, Gervais, Allen, Campomizzi, & Klein, 2012 [4], Psychological Science, 10.1177/0956797611434748, coded as sibling target_index 0) is a separate earlier study that did not counterbalance stimulus orientation and found no inversion effect for female targets; [5] is an independent published study with new experiments, different coauthors, and distinct empirical findings. No prior adjudication or state files exist.
